outcome_mode_directives.create_issue:
## Work mode: create issues

For each distinct finding, file a Pi Dash issue with the `pidash` CLI:
    pidash issue create --project <PROJ> --title "<short summary>" \
        --description "<file path, line range, evidence, severity, suggested fix>"
Before creating an issue, list existing open issues and skip any finding that already has a corresponding open issue (de-dupe by file + root cause, not by exact title). Do NOT modify code.
outcome_mode_directives.apply_fix:
## Work mode: apply fix

For each finding you are confident about, implement the fix and open a pull request for human review — do NOT merge it. Keep one PR per logical fix where practical. If a fix is risky, ambiguous, or larger than a focused change, do NOT force it: create a Pi Dash issue describing the finding instead (same form as create-issue mode).
outcome_mode_directives.fix_and_review:
## Work mode: file issue and delegate fix

Do NOT modify code or open a pull request in this run — the fix is delegated to the issue agent. For each distinct finding, do ALL of the following:
1. File a Pi Dash issue with the `pidash` CLI (de-dupe against existing open issues by file + root cause, as in create-issue mode), and note the issue identifier it returns. Write the description so an AI agent can implement the fix without re-investigating: file path(s) and line range, the evidence you observed, root cause, severity, a concrete suggested fix, and how to validate it:
    pidash issue create --project <PROJ> --title "<short summary>" \
        --description "<agent-ready technical details>"
2. Move the issue to In Progress — this automatically delegates it to the coding agent, which implements the fix and opens a pull request for human review:
    pidash issue patch <IDENT> --state "In Progress"
If a finding is risky, ambiguous, or larger than a focused change, still file the issue but leave it in its default state (do NOT move it to In Progress) and describe the open questions in the issue description instead.
